case_title: UMAKANT & ANR. v. STATE OF CHHATISGARH
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 3, 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 304-B, 302/34 IPC and 498-A IPC
high_court_outcome: Acquitted under Sections 304-B and 498-A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, but convicted under Sections 302/34 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who were the husband and in-laws of the victim, were alleged to have harassed the victim for dowry and subjected her to cruelty and torture. On the day of the incident, the husband poured kerosene on the victim's body, and the mother-in-law set her ablaze. The victim was taken to a hospital where she later succumbed to her injuries. The victim's dying declaration, which was recorded by the magistrate, was the main evidence against the accused. The trial court convicted the accused under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Dowry Prohibition Act. However, the High Court acquitted the accused of some charges but convicted them under Section 302/34 IPC based on the dying declaration. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's conviction, finding that the dying declaration was not reliable and was likely influenced by the family members of the victim.
